memories.statement: Never use em dashes in anything written for me. Commas or a full stop instead.
memories.source: please stop with the long dashes. use a comma or just start a new sentence, i hate how they look

memories.statement: Write at about an eighth grade reading level, plain words over clever ones.
memories.source: keep the words simple. if a normal person wouldnt say it out loud dont write it

memories.statement: It is fine to start a sentence with But, And or So.
memories.source: starting with but is fine btw, i do it when i talk

memories.statement: Prefers repeating the same plain word twice over reaching for a fancier synonym.
memories.source: if the word is slow just say slow again, dont go find sluggish

memories.statement: Wants hedges like I think or seems to be left in, not edited out into confident claims.
memories.source: the softeners are on purpose. seems to be, i feel, that kind of thing. leave them

memories.statement: Dislikes metaphors in technical writing, wants the actual mechanism described.
memories.source: no ships sailing, no orchestras. just say what the code does

memories.statement: Bullet lists should be under six items, otherwise turn them into prose.
memories.source: keep any list under six items. past that turn it into sentences, remember that

memories.statement: Never sign commits or pull request text as a co-author on their behalf.
memories.source: do not put yourself as coauthor on my commits, thats a compliance thing at work not a preference

memories.statement: Commit messages are imperative mood, one line, no body unless something is genuinely non obvious.
memories.source: commit subject imperative. add, fix, drop. body only if future me would be confused

memories.statement: Works from a home desk in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, IST, and most deep work happens between 6am and 10am.
memories.source: mornings are the only time my brain works, 6 to 10, after that its meetings and mush

memories.statement: Will not take meetings before 10am unless it is a production incident.
memories.source: anything before 10 gets declined unless prod is on fire

memories.statement: Vegetarian, eats eggs, does not eat fish or chicken even when travelling.
memories.source: veg but i do eat eggs. no fish. people always assume fish is ok in kerala, its not for me

memories.statement: Lactose does not agree with them past about one cup of milk a day, curd is fine though.
memories.source: milk more than a cup and my stomach is done. curd somehow is fine, no idea why

memories.statement: Drinks filter coffee twice a day and nothing with caffeine after 3pm.
memories.source: two filter coffees, morning and around 2. after 3 nothing or i just lie awake

memories.statement: Uses Neovim for everything except when a debugger is needed, then VS Code.
memories.source: nvim daily driver. i only open vscode when i need to step through something

memories.statement: Terminal is Ghostty with zsh, and tmux for anything long running.
memories.source: switched to ghostty in feb, zsh, tmux for the long stuff

memories.statement: Prefers tabs in Go and two space indents everywhere else.
memories.source: go gets tabs obviously, everything else 2 spaces. 4 feels like shouting

memories.statement: Wants code comments only where the reason is not obvious, never comments that restate the line.
memories.source: dont write // increment i. write why we skip the first row

memories.statement: Hates being given three options when one is clearly better, wants a recommendation with the reason.
memories.source: dont give me a menu. pick one and tell me why, ill argue if i disagree

memories.statement: Wants to be told when something they asked for is a bad idea, even if they pushed for it.
memories.source: if im wrong say so early. i would rather be annoyed now than stuck friday

memories.statement: Reads long answers badly on the phone, so keep the first paragraph enough to act on.
memories.source: half the time im reading this on my phone in a cab. front load it

memories.statement: Prefers a diagram or a small worked example over a paragraph of explanation.
memories.source: draw it. even ascii. i just understand pictures faster than text

memories.statement: Full legal name on documents is spelled with a single r in the middle and people keep doubling it.
memories.source: its one r not two, every insurance form gets it wrong and then the claim bounces

memories.statement: Blood group is O positive.
memories.source: o positive, wrote it on the race form again

memories.statement: Allergic to sulfa drugs, it showed up as a rash when they were nineteen.
memories.source: sulfa is a no. had a rash for a week in college and the doctor wrote it in the file

memories.statement: Wears contacts on run days and glasses the rest of the time.
memories.source: contacts only when i run, otherwise glasses, cant be bothered

memories.statement: Prefers UPI for anything under five thousand rupees and the credit card above that for the points.
memories.source: upi for small stuff, card above 5k so the points add up

memories.statement: Banks with HDFC for salary and keeps a separate current account for the side product money.
memories.source: salary goes to hdfc, side stuff has its own account so i dont mix them at tax time

memories.statement: Will not install an app when the website works, especially for banks and airlines.
memories.source: if the site works im not installing the app. they all want my contacts

memories.statement: Turns off notifications for everything except calls from family and PagerDuty.
memories.source: phone is silent except amma, appa and pagerduty. thats it

memories.statement: Keeps a paper notebook for the day's three things and everything else goes digital.
memories.source: three things on paper every morning, rest lives in the tool

memories.statement: Says they are bad at remembering names and wants people's roles repeated when mentioned.
memories.source: remind me who someone is when you bring them up, im terrible with names

memories.statement: Dates should be written as 14 Mar 2026, never 03/14 or 14/03, because the ambiguity has bitten them.
memories.source: write dates like 14 Mar 2026. the slash format caused a real mess with a vendor once

memories.statement: Money in rupees should be written with the Indian comma grouping, 1,25,000 not 125,000.
memories.source: lakh grouping please. 1,25,000. the other way reads wrong to me

memories.statement: Timezones in anything shared with the team get written as IST with the UTC offset in brackets.
memories.source: always say IST and the utc offset, half the team is in lisbon now

memories.statement: Does not want to be called by a nickname in anything written for other people.
memories.source: full name in writing to others. the short version is for friends

memories.statement: Gets migraines roughly once a month, usually after a bad night, and screens make it worse.
memories.source: the headache thing showed up again. once a month more or less, always after bad sleep

memories.statement: Sleep target is seven and a half hours and they know they get about six on weeknights.
memories.source: i need 7.5, i get 6. thats the whole problem in one line

memories.statement: Cannot work with music that has words in it, instrumental or nothing.
memories.source: lyrics kill it for me. instrumental or silence

memories.statement: Prefers to be given the answer first and the reasoning after, not the other way round.
memories.source: answer first then tell me how you got there. i read the top and decide if i care about the rest

memories.statement: Thinks apologising in chat replies is a waste of a line, just fix the thing.
memories.source: stop saying sorry, just say what changed

memories.statement: Wants numbers rounded sensibly in prose but exact in tables.
memories.source: in a sentence say about 4 lakh. in the table give me the actual number

memories.statement: Prefers Postgres over anything else and is suspicious of new databases without a reason.
memories.source: default to postgres in anything you suggest to me. i need a real reason to move off it

memories.statement: Does not like mocks in tests, prefers a real database in a container.
memories.source: note this one, no mocks. real pg in docker, it takes 2 seconds

memories.statement: Writes tests for the bug first, then the fix, and considers a fix without a test unfinished.
memories.source: test that fails, then the fix. otherwise i dont believe it

memories.statement: Rents, does not own a house, and is not planning to buy in Bengaluru at current prices.
memories.source: everyone asks when im buying. at these prices, never, the rent is a third of the emi

memories.statement: Parents live in Chennai and they visit roughly every two months.
memories.source: chennai trip again in a few weeks, i go every couple of months

memories.statement: Younger sister Meera is doing her masters in Manipal and calls on Sunday evenings.
memories.source: meera calls sunday evenings, she is in manipal till next june

memories.statement: Speaks Malayalam at home, Tamil with neighbours, and writes only in English.
memories.source: malayalam at home, tamil outside, but i cant write either properly

memories.statement: Has a mild fear of driving at night on highways after an incident on the Mysore road.
memories.source: i dont drive highways after dark anymore, not since the mysore road thing

memories.statement: Prefers trains over flights for anything under eight hours when the timing works.
memories.source: if the train is under 8 hours ill take the train, airports eat the time anyway

memories.statement: Keeps passwords in 1Password and will not type a credential into a chat or a shared doc.
memories.source: everything is in 1password. never paste a key into a doc, i will find out

memories.statement: Wants secrets referenced by name, never by value, in anything generated for them.
memories.source: reference the env var name not the value, always

memories.statement: Thinks most meetings should have been a written update and says so often.
memories.source: again a meeting that was three sentences. write it down instead

memories.statement: Prefers async written updates in the morning over standups.
memories.source: let me type my update at 9 and skip the call

memories.statement: Gets restless on calls longer than 45 minutes and will start doing other work.
memories.source: past 45 min on a call im not there anymore, im answering slack

memories.statement: Does not want emojis in anything written for them, in chat or in documents.
memories.source: no emojis please, it makes serious things look cheap

memories.statement: Used to be fine with emoji in Slack reactions but now finds even that noisy.
memories.source: i used to say reactions are fine but honestly even those are noise now

memories.statement: Keeps a running list of words they overuse, currently just, actually, and basically.
memories.source: im overusing just and basically again, call it out if you see it

memories.statement: Calls the coffee shop below the flat Third Wave and goes there when the house is too quiet.
memories.source: went down to third wave to work, house was too quiet today

memories.statement: Right handed but mouses with the left hand because of an old wrist problem.
memories.source: mouse is on the left, wrist thing from 2021, everyone asks

memories.statement: Uses a split keyboard and cannot type properly on a laptop keyboard for more than an hour.
memories.source: the split board ruined me for laptop typing, an hour and my shoulders are up at my ears

memories.statement: Deletes email rather than archiving, and keeps the inbox under twenty.
memories.source: i delete. archive is just a landfill with better branding

memories.statement: Will not sign up for anything that needs a phone number if email works.
memories.source: not giving my number to another startup, email or nothing

memories.statement: Thinks in terms of what breaks at 10x, and asks that question of every design.
memories.source: always ask what happens at 10x. if the answer is we rewrite it, fine, but say it now

memories.statement: Prefers boring technology and says the exciting part should be the product not the stack.
memories.source: boring stack, interesting product. thats the whole philosophy

memories.statement: Will not work on anything gambling or lending adjacent, turned down a job over it in 2024.
memories.source: no betting, no predatory lending. said no to a good offer over that and id do it again

memories.statement: Budget for tools is about two thousand rupees a month and anything above needs a real reason.
memories.source: i give myself 2k a month for software, past that i have to justify it to myself

memories.statement: Keeps Sunday afternoons free of anything scheduled, that is the rule they break least.
memories.source: sunday afternoon is nothing. no calls no errands. its the one thing i actually hold

memories.statement: Fasts from screens on Sunday from about noon until evening.
memories.source: trying no screens sunday afternoon, its been about six weeks now

memories.statement: Wants long documents to open with what changed and what they need to decide.
memories.source: top of any doc: whats different and what do you want from me. rest can be below

memories.statement: Prefers the word wrong over incorrect and broken over degraded.
memories.source: say broken not degraded. degraded is what you write when you dont want to admit it

memories.statement: Asks for the file path every time so they can jump straight there.
memories.source: always give me the path, full path, i keep having to ask

memories.statement: Gets seasonal allergies in October and November, mostly in the mornings.
memories.source: october again, nose is gone by 7am every day

memories.statement: Thinks their own writing gets worse when they try to sound smart and wants it kept a bit unpolished.
memories.source: leave it slightly rough. every time i polish it starts sounding like linkedin

memories.statement: Has a standing rule not to ship anything to production on a Friday after 2pm.
memories.source: nothing goes out friday afternoon. learnt that the hard way in 2024

memories.statement: Cardinal is a Go service and the team agreed to stay on Go 1.23 until the payout migration is finished.
memories.source: we are not bumping go until payouts are done. ritu was firm about it

memories.statement: Ritu Sabharwal is the tech lead on Cardinal and reviews anything that touches double entry booking.
memories.source: ritu has to look at anything near the booking code, thats the rule she set

memories.statement: Fahad on SRE owns the pgbouncer config and should be pinged before any pool change.
memories.source: fahad owns pgbouncer, ping him first, i learnt that after the feb thing

memories.statement: Every money amount inside Cardinal is stored in paise as an int64, never a float, never a decimal string.
memories.source: paise, int64, everywhere. if you see a float in the money path thats a bug not a style choice

memories.statement: Ledger entries are append only and nothing is ever updated in place, corrections are new reversing entries.
memories.source: we never update a row in entries. you write the opposite entry. thats the whole model

memories.statement: The service handles about 2.4 million bookings a day with a peak around 9pm IST.
memories.source: 2.4m a day now, peak is 9pm, food delivery merchants mostly

memories.statement: p99 on the capture endpoint should stay under 180ms and it sat around 240ms through July.
memories.source: slo is 180 on capture, we were at 240 all july and nobody said anything

memories.statement: The repo is github.com/vellum-pay/cardinal and the main branch is protected with two approvals.
memories.source: cardinal repo needs two approvals on main now, slowed everything down but fair

memories.statement: Integration tests run against a real Postgres in Docker and take about four minutes locally.
memories.source: make test spins up pg, four minutes, i usually go make coffee

memories.statement: There is a soak test environment called kestrel that mirrors production traffic at ten percent.
memories.source: kestrel is the soak env, 10 percent shadow traffic. use it before anything risky goes out

memories.statement: Idempotency keys should be scoped to merchant plus key, not global, because two merchants reuse the same UUIDs.
memories.source: scope the key by merchant. two of our merchants literally send the same uuids, saw it in the logs

memories.statement: Idempotency records expire after 48 hours, which was chosen to match the longest retry window a client uses.
memories.source: 48 hours on the idempotency rows. thats the longest anyone retries, checked with the top ten merchants

memories.statement: The stored response body for a replayed request must be byte identical, not regenerated.
memories.source: store the actual bytes we sent. dont re render it, the timestamps drift and clients diff it

memories.statement: Sneha wants the replayed response to carry a header saying it was a replay, ops asked for that.
memories.source: sneha wants an x-replayed header so support can tell. easy enough

memories.statement: Concurrent requests with the same idempotency key should return 409 while the first is in flight, not block.
memories.source: if two land at once the second gets a 409 conflict. blocking just moves the pileup

memories.statement: The settlement retry worker uses exponential backoff with full jitter and caps at fifteen minutes.
memories.source: full jitter, cap 15 min. the AWS blog post one, not the half jitter variant

memories.statement: Before the backoff change, retries were clustering every sixty seconds and hammering the bank partner.
memories.source: everything retried at exactly 60s so we sent the partner a wall of traffic once a minute. embarrassing

memories.statement: The bank partner rate limit is 40 requests per second per merchant and they do not publish it anywhere.
memories.source: 40 rps per merchant, we found out by getting throttled, its not in their docs

memories.statement: After the jitter change, failed settlement volume dropped from about 3,200 a day to under 400.
memories.source: 3200 failures a day down to like 380. best two line change ive shipped

memories.statement: The legacy payouts_v1 table cannot be dropped until finance signs off on the seven year retention question.
memories.source: cant drop payouts_v1, legal says seven years and nobody has confirmed the archive covers it

memories.statement: payouts_v1 has 41 million rows and two views still reading from it that nobody owns.
memories.source: 41m rows and two views pointing at it, git blame says a guy who left in 2023

memories.statement: The backfill from payouts_v1 to the new table finished in April and the row counts matched exactly.
memories.source: backfill done april, counts matched to the row which honestly surprised me

memories.statement: Pool sizes ended at 25 per instance with a max of 300 across the fleet, decided with Fahad.
memories.source: 25 per pod, 300 total, fahad worked it back from the pg max_connections

memories.statement: The pool starvation only showed up during the 9pm peak and looked like random timeouts for weeks.
memories.source: it only broke at 9pm so it looked random. took three weeks to see the pattern

memories.statement: Transaction mode pooling broke prepared statements and they had to turn off statement caching in the driver.
memories.source: transaction pooling killed prepared stmts, had to disable the cache in pgx. cost us maybe 4 percent

memories.statement: Webhook signatures use HMAC SHA256 over the raw body with a five minute timestamp tolerance.
memories.source: hmac sha256 on the raw bytes, 5 min tolerance on the timestamp

memories.statement: Signature comparison must be constant time and there is at least one place in the codebase using plain equality.
memories.source: found a == on a signature in the partner callback handler. thats the actual thing to fix

memories.statement: Three merchants are still on the old signing key and cannot be rotated until they redeploy.
memories.source: three merchants on the old key. one of them says their dev left. wonderful

memories.statement: Partial refunds must never let the total refunded exceed the captured amount, enforced in the database not the app.
memories.source: put the check constraint in pg. app level checks lose races, we already proved that

memories.statement: A partial refund books two entries, a debit to the merchant balance and a credit to the refund clearing account.
memories.source: debit merchant, credit refund clearing. same as full refund just smaller

memories.statement: Karthik found that the refund API already accepts an amount field that has been silently ignored since 2024.
memories.source: karthik found we take an amount param on refunds and just ignore it. some merchants have been sending it for two years

memories.statement: The March incident was caused by a settlement job running twice after a Kubernetes rollout, not by the code.
memories.source: march outage was a double run during a rollout. the code was fine, the deploy wasnt

memories.statement: The runbook now starts with how to stop the settlement worker, because that is the first thing anyone needs.
memories.source: put the kill switch at the top of the runbook. nobody reads past the first screen at 3am

memories.statement: On call rotation is one week, handover is Wednesday 11am, and there are six people in it.
memories.source: week long rotation, handover wednesday 11, six of us

memories.statement: Balance caching is risky because ops reads balances right after a write and expects them to be right.
memories.source: the problem with caching balance is support refreshes the page immediately after and screenshots the wrong number

memories.statement: Reads of merchant balance are about 90 percent of all ledger queries.
memories.source: 90 percent of our reads are just what is this merchants balance. thats why im even thinking about a cache

memories.statement: The team writes design docs in Notion but the decision record lives in the repo as a numbered ADR.
memories.source: notion for the discussion, adr in the repo for the decision. otherwise notion eats it

memories.statement: Feature flags go through LaunchDarkly and every flag needs an owner and a removal date in the description.
memories.source: every flag gets an owner and a date it dies. we had 140 flags last year, it was a swamp

memories.statement: Deploys happen twice a day at 11am and 4pm IST and nothing goes out on Fridays after lunch.
memories.source: write this down, deploy windows are 11 and 4 ist, and friday afternoon is frozen

memories.statement: Database migrations are forward only and a rollback means writing a new migration.
memories.source: no down migrations. if you need to undo it you write a new one

memories.statement: Anything that adds a column must ship with a default or it locks the table, learnt in the Feb outage.
memories.source: add column without a default and pg rewrites the table. we took prod down for eleven minutes learning that

memories.statement: Error wrapping uses fmt.Errorf with %w and never errors.New in a code path that crosses a package boundary.
memories.source: %w always, so the caller can check. errors.New only for sentinel values

memories.statement: Logging is structured JSON with slog and the merchant id goes on every line as a field not in the message.
memories.source: merchant_id is a field not part of the string. grep is not a log system

memories.statement: Metrics live in Prometheus, dashboards in Grafana, and traces in Tempo, all self hosted.
memories.source: prom, grafana, tempo, all ours. datadog quote was 40 lakh a year

memories.statement: Ana Marques joined from Lisbon in June and is ramping on the settlement side.
memories.source: ana started in june, lisbon, she is picking up settlement. good questions so far

memories.statement: Lisbon overlap is only about three hours a day so anything for Ana needs to be written down.
memories.source: we get maybe 3 hours with lisbon. if its not written ana doesnt get it

memories.statement: The settlement file format the bank expects is fixed width and one wrong space rejects the whole file.
memories.source: fixed width, and if one field is off by a space the bank rejects the entire batch, no partial

memories.statement: Settlement cutoff is 6pm IST and anything after goes the next working day, which merchants never remember.
memories.source: 6pm cutoff. every single merchant asks why their money moved tomorrow

memories.statement: Thinks the ledger should eventually be its own service separate from the payments API but there is no appetite.
memories.source: i keep saying split the ledger out. nobody wants to hear it this quarter

memories.statement: Quarterly planning happens in the first week of the quarter and Sneha runs it.
memories.source: planning first week, sneha runs it, bring numbers not feelings

memories.statement: Orbit is Next.js 15 on the app router with server components for everything that is not interactive.
memories.source: app router, server components by default, client only where you actually click things

memories.statement: Styling is Tailwind with a small set of design tokens, no component library.
memories.source: tailwind plus our own tokens. we tried shadcn and ended up fighting it

memories.statement: Dark mode is the default because ops sit in a dim room on night shift.
memories.source: dark is default. the night shift folks asked and honestly they are right

memories.statement: There were 74 hardcoded hex colours before the token cleanup and eleven of them were nearly the same grey.
memories.source: 74 hex values in the codebase. eleven shades of almost the same grey. how

memories.statement: Tokens are named by role like surface, surface-raised, text-muted, not by colour name.
memories.source: name them by what they do not what they look like. no more slate-700 in jsx

memories.statement: The Rust project is a key value store with a write ahead log, built purely to learn the language.
memories.source: its a kv store with a wal. nobody will use it, thats fine, its a language exercise

memories.statement: Works on it on weeknights after dinner, usually an hour, three or four nights a week.
memories.source: an hour after dinner, three or four nights. slow but it adds up

memories.statement: Each WAL record is a length prefix, a CRC32 checksum, then the payload.
memories.source: length, crc32, payload. same shape as most wals, no point inventing

memories.statement: Decided to fsync on every write for now and measure before making it configurable.
memories.source: fsync every write. i know its slow. measure first then decide, otherwise its just cargo culting

memories.statement: The in memory index is a BTreeMap from key to file offset, rebuilt on startup by replaying the log.
memories.source: btreemap key to offset, replay the log on boot to build it. simple and it works

memories.statement: Got stuck for two evenings on borrowing the writer while also reading the index, solved it by splitting the struct.
memories.source: two nights fighting the borrow checker. answer was my struct was doing two jobs. splitting it fixed everything

memories.statement: Recovery should stop at the first bad checksum and treat everything after as lost, not try to skip ahead.
memories.source: first bad crc, stop, truncate there. trying to skip past corruption is how you get silent garbage

memories.statement: Plans to test recovery by truncating the log file at random byte offsets in a loop.
memories.source: just chop the file at random offsets a thousand times and check it always comes up clean

memories.statement: The LSM paper from 1996 was clearer than most blog posts written about it since.
memories.source: the actual 96 paper is easier to read than the blog posts explaining it. that keeps happening

memories.statement: Took away from the LSM paper that the whole idea is turning random writes into sequential ones.
memories.source: the one idea is random writes become sequential writes. everything else is bookkeeping

memories.statement: Lifetimes finally made sense when they stopped reading them as duration and started reading them as scope of validity.
memories.source: lifetimes clicked when i stopped thinking how long and started thinking valid where

memories.statement: Wrote that clone is fine while learning and optimising it away early just slows the learning down.
memories.source: just clone it. you can take the clones out later. fighting it on day one is how people quit rust

memories.statement: Uses no external crates except anyhow and crc32fast, on purpose.
memories.source: only anyhow and crc32fast. the whole point is doing it myself

memories.statement: Finds Rust error messages genuinely helpful, unlike the C++ ones they grew up with.
memories.source: the compiler actually tells you what to do. after c++ templates this feels like cheating

memories.statement: Does not want to use async in this project, blocking IO keeps it understandable.
memories.source: no tokio. blocking io. i want to understand what the machine is doing

memories.statement: The repo is private and will probably stay that way until the recovery tests pass.
memories.source: not putting it on github until crash recovery actually works. no need for that embarrassment

memories.statement: Thinks about six months in that Rust is slower to write and easier to trust, and that trade is worth it.
memories.source: its slower to write and i trust it more. for a database thats the right trade

memories.source: the wal stuff and the idempotency post are the same idea really. exactly once is a lie, at least once plus dedupe is the truth
